title: Extension by the empty set of a sheaf of sets along an open subset
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space (presheaves and sheaves of sets on $X$ are those on the site of open subsets of $X$ with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]), $U\subseteq X$ an open subset with inclusion $j_U:U\to X$, and $\mathcal G$ a sheaf of sets on $U$. The presheaf of sets $j_{U,p!}\mathcal G$ on $X$ is defined by $(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)(V)=\mathcal G(V)$ if $V\subseteq U$ and $(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)(V)=\emptyset$ if $V\not\subseteq U$ ($V\subseteq X$ open); for opens $V'\subseteq V$ the restriction map is the restriction map of $\mathcal G$ when $V\subseteq U$ (then $V'\subseteq U$), and the empty map when $V\not\subseteq U$. The *extension of $\mathcal G$ by the empty set* is the sheaf of sets $j_{U!}\mathcal G$ on $X$ given by the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] $j_{U,p!}\mathcal G\to j_{U!}\mathcal G$. A morphism $\alpha:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ of sheaves on $U$ gives $j_{U,p!}\alpha$ (equal to $\alpha_V$ on $V\subseteq U$, empty otherwise) and hence $j_{U!}\alpha$. For a set $S$ write $\underline S_U$ for the sheaf of sets on $U$ with $\underline S_U(V)=\{$locally constant maps $V\to S\}$ ($V\subseteq U$ open, restriction of maps), and $j_{U!}\underline S:=j_{U!}(\underline S_U)$.

source.place: Sheaves, Section 'Open immersions and (pre)sheaves of sets' (Tag 009Z), Definition Tag 00A2 (label definition-j-shriek, line 4525); notation j_{U!} and the constant sheaf as in Modules, Section 'Constructible sheaves of sets' (Tag 0CAG, modules.tex line 2979)

proof.text: (The presheaf $j_{U,p!}\mathcal G$.) The rule is well defined: if $V\subseteq U$ and $V'\subseteq V$ then $V'\subseteq U$, so the restriction $\mathcal G(V)\to\mathcal G(V')$ lands in $(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)(V')$; if $V\not\subseteq U$ the source is $\emptyset$ and the empty map $\emptyset\to(j_{U,p!}\mathcal G)(V')$ is the only map. Functoriality: the restriction for $V=V'$ is the identity (that of $\mathcal G$, or $\mathrm{id}_\emptyset$); for $V''\subseteq V'\subseteq V$ the composite equals the restriction $V\to V''$: if $V\subseteq U$ all three are restrictions of $\mathcal G$, which compose; if $V\not\subseteq U$ both sides are maps out of $\emptyset$, hence equal. So $j_{U,p!}\mathcal G$ is a presheaf of sets on $X$ (Stacks: 'with obvious restriction mappings'). (Whether $j_{U,p!}\mathcal G$ is already a sheaf is not needed: Stacks sheafifies in any case, step 2.)

(The sheaf $j_{U!}\mathcal G$.) The open subsets of $X$ with open coverings form a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and every presheaf of sets on it has a sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; $j_{U!}\mathcal G$ is the sheafification of the presheaf of step 1, together with $\theta_{\mathcal G}:j_{U,p!}\mathcal G\to j_{U!}\mathcal G$. It is unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with $\theta$ by its universal property, so the definition does not depend on the choice.

source.place: Definition Tag 00A2 (2); sheafification: Section Tag 007X (section-sheafification), Lemma Tag 0080 (lemma-sheafify-universal)

proof.text: (Functoriality.) For $\alpha:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ the family $(j_{U,p!}\alpha)_V=\alpha_V$ ($V\subseteq U$), the empty map $\emptyset\to\emptyset$ ($V\not\subseteq U$), is a natural transformation: for $V'\subseteq V$ with $V\subseteq U$ this is the naturality of $\alpha$, and for $V\not\subseteq U$ both composites are maps out of $\emptyset$. Clearly $j_{U,p!}\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{id}$ and $j_{U,p!}(\beta\alpha)=j_{U,p!}\beta\circ j_{U,p!}\alpha$. By the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] there is exactly one $j_{U!}\alpha:j_{U!}\mathcal G\to j_{U!}\mathcal G'$ with $j_{U!}\alpha\circ\theta_{\mathcal G}=\theta_{\mathcal G'}\circ j_{U,p!}\alpha$, and this uniqueness gives $j_{U!}\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{id}$ and $j_{U!}(\beta\alpha)=j_{U!}\beta\circ j_{U!}\alpha$. So $j_{U,p!}$ and $j_{U!}$ are functors.

source.place: Definition Tag 00A2; functoriality of sheafification as in Section Tag 007X (section-sheafification)

proof.text: (The sheaf $\underline S_U$.) For a set $S$ (discrete topology) a map $V\to S$ is locally constant iff it is continuous, and continuous maps glue: given an open cover $V=\bigcup V_i$ and locally constant $f_i:V_i\to S$ agreeing on overlaps there is exactly one $f:V\to S$ restricting to the $f_i$, and it is locally constant since being locally constant is a local property. Restriction of maps is functorial. So $\underline S_U$ is a sheaf of sets on $U$ (its value on $\emptyset$ is the one-point set $\{\emptyset\to S\}$), and $j_{U!}\underline S:=j_{U!}(\underline S_U)$ is defined by step 2. This is the constant sheaf of Stacks 006W on the space $U$, and the notation $j_{U!}\underline S$ is that of Modules, Section 0CAG.

proof.text: (What the definition does not contain.) The properties Stacks proves right after Definition 00A2, Lemma 00A3: $j_{U,p!}$ and $j_{U!}$ are left adjoint to the restriction to $U$, the stalks of $j_{U!}\mathcal G$ are $\emptyset$ off $U$ and $\mathcal G_x$ on $U$, and $\mathcal G\to(j_{U!}\mathcal G)|_U$ is an isomorphism, are not part of the definition and are not used in steps 1-4; they are the separate statement lem-weil-pbc-sets-extension-by-empty-adjunction (created by this split, unsplit; Stacks Modules 0CAH uses its adjunction and stalk parts, so lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-directed-colimit-finite-coequalizers and the statements built on Tag 0CAH should cite it). It is not listed in uses because it depends on this definition. Stacks' remark after 00A3 that $j_!$ of an abelian sheaf is not abelian (empty stalks) is why the abelian version is extension by zero, here [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] for etale modules (Definition Tag 00A4 in the topological case); that node is not used here.
